title: Attan circle dance (Pashtun round dance)
summary: Attan is the round dance of the Pashtun people of Afghanistan and Pakistan. Dancers circle about the dhol drummer, clapping and stepping in time, and as the drum quickens each dancer spins about his own axis, his wide shirt and long hair flying.
howToPlay: Eight dancers circle the dhol drum on a woven carpet. Lit places between them are Clap, Step, Hop and Spin; Dhol is the drum itself in the middle.
A ring closes on a place when it is time. Clap, step, hop and spin as the ring closes and the circle answers.
Begin with the steady round, then try the quickening round.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the tradition, not transcriptions.
heritageNote: Attan is danced at weddings and festivals; the dhol starts slowly and quickens until the dancers are spinning.
